en.title: Remarks by Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs, at the handing over ceremony of the India-Maldives Friendship Faculty of Hospitality and Tourism Building
en.description: Minister of External Affairs of India, His Excellency Mr. Salman Khurshid,
en.body:
Minister of External Affairs of India, His Excellency Mr. Salman Khurshid,

Chancellor at the Maldives National University, Dr Mohamed Zahir Hussain,  
  
Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen  
  
Assalaam Alaikum,  
  
  
  
I am honoured to accept on behalf of the Government of Maldives, the India-Maldives Friendship Faculty of Hospitality and Tourism Building. I would like to thank Your Excellency and the Government of India for this generous assistance to the Maldives. The India-Maldives Friendship Faculty of Hospitality and Tourism Building has been a long standing commitment. Today, we are happy to see its completion, with fully functional classrooms and computer labs that would cater for almost 200 full time students.  
  
  
  
This creates more opportunities for Maldivian students to stay in the country and pursue quality higher education in the field of hospitality and tourism. This will also lead to the generation of a qualified workforce for the tourism and hospitality industry of the Maldives.  
  
  
  
Excellencies,  
  
  
  
It is indeed no exaggeration when I say that the strong bonds between the Maldives and India go way back in time. Next year the Maldives will be celebrating 50 years since our independence. It is against this backdrop that we will also be celebrating, 50 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Maldives and India.Our relationship is based on mutual understanding and respect for each other's sovereignty.The historical and cultural friendship and cooperation between our two countries are evident not only in the partnership between our two Governments, but also in the close ties between our peoples.  
  
  
  
Today we see that the relationship between our two countries is continuing to grow from strength to strength. India continues to be a close partner of the Maldives in diverse spheres; be it, development, economic, social, cultural or security. I would therefore like to take this opportunity to express our appreciation to India for its readiness to assist the Maldives in its times of need.  
  
  
  
Excellencies,  
  
  
  
Over the years India has shown tremendous amount of generosity towards the Maldives. Indira Gandhi Memorial Hospital and the Faculty of Engineering Technology stand as the most visible icons of our close friendship. This Building, which is a new icon of our ties, shows the commitment of the Indian Government towards assisting the Maldives in developing our infrastructure and strengthening our human resource capacity.  
  
  
  
Therefore, I take this opportunity to reiterate the profound appreciation of the Government and the people of the Maldives to the Government and people of India for the warmth you have shown in your relationship with the Maldives, and fro the continued support and assistance towards all our development efforts.  
  
  
  
Excellency,  
  
  
  
I have no doubt that this traditional bond of friendship and cooperation that we have enjoyed over the past will continue to grow and expand in the years to come.  
  
  
  
Thank you!

en.title: Conclusion of the Forty Fifth Session of the Programming Committee
en.description: 18February 2014, Maldives; The Forty Fifth Session of the Programming Committee successfully concluded yesterday.Items stated in the Committee's report , as part of theworks undertakenincludes, inter alia,review of the…
en.body:
18February 2014, Maldives; The Forty Fifth Session of the Programming Committee successfully concluded yesterday.Items stated in the Committee's report , as part of theworks undertakenincludes, inter alia,review of the status of the implementation ofthe recommendation of the Forty Forth Session of Programming Committee; consideration of the Report of the Seventh Meeting of the Working Group on Energy; consideration of the Report of the Technical Committee on Environment and Forestry;consideration of the compilation of all rules, regulations, orders and decisions pertaining to the Administrative and Financial Matters and Provisions of the Secretariat; consideration of the SAARC's Calendar and the recommendations and comments forwarded by the Committee in respect of the foregoing matters.

Chairman of the Committee Mr. Hassan Shifau briefed the local media immediately following the conclusion of the session.  
  
  
  
Also, later in the evening, Chairman of the Forty Fifth Session of the Programming Committee H E Mr Hassan Shifau hosted a dinner in honor of the delegates of the SAARC's Member states.  
  
  
  
Concurrently, on the sidelines of the Programming Committee the Foreign Secretary of the Republic of India H.E.S.M.T. Sujatha Singh paid a courtesy call on the Foreign Secretary of the Maldives, Dr. Ali Mohamed Naseer, at Funamaa Lounge of Bandos Island Resort. The discussions between the counterparts mainly focused on the upcoming Thirty Fifth Session of the Council of Ministers, and the scheduled official visit of the Minister External Affairs of India.  
  
  
  
ENDS

en.title: The Sixth Special Session Of The Standing Committee Begins Today
en.description: 18 February 2014, Maldives; The Sixth Special Session of the Standing Committeebegins today in Bandos Island Resort, the Maldives.
en.body:
18 February 2014, Maldives; The Sixth Special Session of the Standing Committeebegins today in Bandos Island Resort, the Maldives.

The Sixth Special Session will principally focus on matters pertaining to cooperation with the SAARC's Observers. As part of its working program, the Sixth Special Session will, inter alia, deliberate on the matter of admitting new Observers to the SAARC.Furthermore, the session will also consider proposals by the People's Republic of China and the Republic of Korea on matters relating to cultural cooperation. The report on the Sixth Special Session is to be adopted at its conclusion.  
  
  
  
The Standing Committee, as provided under the SAARC Charter, is comprised of the Foreign Secretaries of the SAARC Member States. To date, the Standing Committee has held five Special Sessions, on a special requirement basis. To this effect, theendorsement by the Council, at its the Thirty-Fourth Session, of the recommendation of the Thirty-ninth Session of the Standing Committee, to review all matters pertaining to SAARC's engagement with its Observers, provides a basis for the Sixth Special Session of the Standing Committee.  
  
  
  
ENDS.

en.title: SAARC Programming Committee begins in Maldives
en.description: 17 February 2014, Male'; The Forty-fifth Session of the SAARC Programming Committee begins in the Maldives today. As part of its working program, the Committee is scheduled to review the status of the implementation of…
en.body:
17 February 2014, Male'; The Forty-fifth Session of the SAARC Programming Committee begins in the Maldives today. As part of its working program, the Committee is scheduled to review the status of the implementation of recommendations provided at the Forty-Fourth Session, in December 2013. Further, the Committee will consider a Report of the Working Group on Energy and a Report of the Technical Committee on Environment and Forestry. The Committee will also consider financial and administrative matters relating to the SAARC's Secretariat, and the SAARC's calendar of activities for the year ahead. The report on the Forty Fifth Session is to be adopted at its conclusion.

As current chairperson of the SAARC, the Government of Maldives will chair the Council of Ministers and its preceding meetings including the Programming Committee. To this effect the Committee will be chaired by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Mr. Hassan Shifau.  
  
The Programming Committee of SAARC effectively monitors the operational running of the Association and to this effect, deliberates on all matters relating to administration, budget and running of the Association. It also monitors the work of the Secretariat in implementing the decisions of the Summit and other meetings. The Maldives Delegation to the Programming Committee is led by Ms. Fathimath Najwa, Assistant Director and Head of SAARC Division in the Ministry.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India to make an official visit to the Maldives
en.description: 13 February 2014, Male': Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India, H.E. Mr. Salman Khurshid, , is scheduled to make an official visit to the Maldives on 19 February 2014 at the invitation of the Minister of…
en.body:
13 February 2014, Male': Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India, H.E. Mr. Salman Khurshid, , is scheduled to make an official visit to the Maldives on 19 February 2014 at the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon.

The visit of Minister Salman Khurshid precedes the 35th Session of the SAARCCouncil of Ministers Meeting to be held in Bandos Island Resort on 20 February 2014. This would be the first official visit of a Foreign Minister received by the new Government of President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom.  
  
  
  
During the visit, both governments will engage in high level official talks, reaffirming the commitments and close cordial relations between the two countries.

en.title: Maldives to host the Thirty-Fifth Session of the SAARC Council of Ministers and its Preceding Meetings
en.description: 13 February 2014, Male'; In its role as current chair of SAARC, the Maldives will host the Thirty-Fifth Session of the SAARC Council of Ministers and its preceding meetings from February 17-20 February 2014. The…
en.body:
13 February 2014, Male'; In its role as current chair of SAARC, the Maldives will host the Thirty-Fifth Session of the SAARC Council of Ministers and its preceding meetings from February 17-20 February 2014. The four-day event is to be held at Bandos Island Resort & Spa.

In accordance with this year's theme, 'Towards Regional Resilience', the Council of Ministers will reflect upon important regional issues including: poverty, agriculture and food security; climate change and environment; education; connectivity; trade and finance; health; combating terrorism and drug trafficking; maritime security and piracy; energy security; and the social sector. In this regard, the session will provide valuable direction for SAARC policy and processes in the years ahead.  
  
  
  
As part of the Session's work program, the Council will consider a comprehensive study to strengthen SAARC mechanisms and decision-making towards furthering the objectives enshrined in the SAARC Charter reforming SAARC processes as a whole. The Council will also review existing guidelines relating to SAARC's engagement with observer countries, in order to maximize the benefits gained from such engagement. Furthermore, the Council will discuss possibilities for fast-tracking projects to promote social and economic development in the region, thereby enabling SAARC to play a greater role in realizing the hopes and aspirations of the people of the region.  
  
  
  
The Thirty-Fifth Session of the SAARC Council of Ministers will be the first occasion the SAARC Foreign Ministers have met since the 17th SAARC Summit, held on 10-11 November 2011.  
  
  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to the Republic of Maldives calls on Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives
en.description: 9 February 2014, Male': His Excellency Dr. Jurgen Morhard, Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to the Republic of Maldives, calls on Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the…
en.body:
9 February 2014, Male': His Excellency Dr. Jurgen Morhard, Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to the Republic of Maldives, calls on Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives today.

During the meeting, held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Foreign Minister and Ambassador discussed ways of further strengthening the existing close relations between the Maldives and Germany with an emphasis on greater cooperation in the field of tourism, education, trade and investment.  
  
  
  
The meeting was attended by Ms. Farzana Zahir, Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives.  
  
  
  
ENDS

en.title: Special Envoy of the President attends the 14th Delhi Sustainable Development Summit
en.description: 6 February 2014, Male; Ambassador at large His Excellency Mr. Abdulla Hameed is attending the 14th Delhi Sustainable Development Summit organized by "The Energy and Resources Institute" as the Special Envoy of the…
en.body:
6 February 2014, Male; Ambassador at large His Excellency Mr. Abdulla Hameed is attending the 14th Delhi Sustainable Development Summit organized by "The Energy and Resources Institute" as the Special Envoy of the President. The Summit convened today at Taj Palace Hotel in New Delhi, India and will continue until 8 February 2014. The summit is a platform to discuss important issues of sustainability and relevant policy interventions to achieve sustainable development goals. This year's theme is "Attaining Energy, Water and Food Security for all".

The Special Envoy is accompanied by Mr. Amjad Abdulla, Director General of Climate Change of the Ministry of Environment and Energy and Ms. Shiuneen Rasheed, Assistant Director of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  
  
Ends

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya Holds Interaction with Maldivians in Malaysia
en.description: 05 February 2014, Male'; The Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon hosted a special function for Maldivian nationals in Malaysia last night. The event, which was held at the Maldives High Commission in…
en.body:
05 February 2014, Male'; The Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon hosted a special function for Maldivian nationals in Malaysia last night. The event, which was held at the Maldives High Commission in Kuala Lumpur, was well attended by Maldivians studying and living in Malaysia.

At the function, the Minister outlined the Government's foreign policy priorities and highlighted the efforts of the Government in providing quality consular service to Maldivians living abroad. In this regard, the Minister announced that due to the recent changes in Malaysian Immigration policies that require all international students to obtain a separate single entry visa after their visa approval is granted, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has made an arrangement to facilitate the acquisition of the single entry visa from Colombo without students having to travel to Sri Lanka. The Foreign Minister also listened to the ideas and concerns of the Maldivians including the challenges they face in their stay and travel to Malaysia.  
  
The Minister is currently on a one-day working visit to Kuala Lumpur and is scheduled to return to Male' tonight after concluding her visit.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs on a Working Visit to Kuala Lumpur
en.description: 04 February 2014, Male';Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, has today met with the staff of the Maldivian High Commission, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The Minister was received at the High Commission by…
en.body:
04 February 2014, Male';Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, has today met with the staff of the Maldivian High Commission, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The Minister was received at the High Commission by the acting High Commissioner of Maldives to Malaysia, Mr. Mohamed Fahmy Hassan.

Minister Dunya is on a one day, working visit to Kuala Lumpur.  
  
At the High Commission, the Minister met with the staff and received a briefing on the current workings and issues relevant to the administration of the High Commission in Malaysia.In her remarks, the Minister underscored that one of the main goals of the Maldives foreign policy is providing quality consular services to Maldivians living abroad. In this regard, the Minister noted that Malaysia is host to a large number of Maldivians and thus, highlighted that the Mission continue its good work in providing quality services to Maldivians living in Malaysia..  
  
During her visit, the Minister, is also scheduled to host a function for a group of Maldivians currently living in Malaysia. The Minister will hold discussions with Maldivians on the challenges faced by Maldivians in their travel and stay in Malaysia. The function will take place at the High Commission premises.  
  
Further to recent amendments brought to the immigration policy, the Immigration Department of Malaysia now requires all international students wishing to study in the country to apply for an Entry Visa upon receiving approval for their Student Visas. Minister Dunya, in order to address this issue, has facilitated for such Maldivian students to process their visas via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs without requiring traveling to Colombo. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has advised such students to apply for their Entry Visas at least 10 days in advance to the Ministry in order to ensure smooth process.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: United Nations Resident Coordinator a.i. and UNDP Resident Representative a.i. calls on the Minister of Foreign Affairs
en.description: 29 January 2014, Male'; Mr. David McLachlan-Karr, United Nations Resident Coordinator a.i. and UNDP Resident Representative a.i., called onHer Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs today.
en.body:
29 January 2014, Male'; Mr. David McLachlan-Karr, United Nations Resident Coordinator a.i. and UNDP Resident Representative a.i., called onHer Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry, Minister Dunya welcomed Mr. McLachlan-Karr to the Maldives and expressed the Government's appreciation for the continued assistance of the United Nations system and particularly the country office. The Minister further briefed the UN Resident Coordinator a.i. on the Government's policies, priorities, including the foreign policy goals and objectives. The Minister expressed hope that the collaboration between the Government and the United Nations Offices in the Maldives would be further strengthened during Mr. McMcLachlan-Karr's tenure.  
  
The United Nations Resident Coordinator a.i. thanked the Minister for the warm welcome and assured that the close working relationship would continue to exist between the Maldives and the United Nations. The Resident Coordinator briefed the Minister on ongoing issues and upcoming projects, as well as exchanged ideas on further strengthening the assistance framework of the United Nations to the Maldives.  
  
Mr. David McLachlan-Karr is an Australian by nationality and took up the post as the United Nations Resident Coordinator and UNDP Resident Representative in Papua New Guinea in 2009. He previously held the post of RC/RR in Venezuela from October 2004.  
  
ENDS

en.title: Maldives and the United States of America signs a Memorandum of Understanding to extend the Fulbright Exchange Program
en.description: 29 January 2014, Male'; The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the United States of America, has today, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to extend the Fulbright Exchange Program for a…
en.body:
29 January 2014, Male'; The Government of the Republic of Maldives and the Government of the United States of America, has today, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to extend the Fulbright Exchange Program for a further period of five years.

The MoU was signed by Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Her Excellency Ms. Michele J. Sison, Ambassador of the United States of America to the Republic of Maldives, on behalf of the Government of Maldives and the Government of the United States, respectively.  
  
The Fulbright Exchange Program is intended to strengthen and develop ties between the Maldives and the United States of America, through academic, professional, and cultural exchanges between the two countries. Through this MoU, over 20 students from the Maldives have completed the Fulbright Masters and the Humphry Fellowship Program, and a number of professionals and researchers from the United States have alsoworked in the Maldives. The Fulbright Exchange Program was initially signed between the Maldives and the United States of America in 2003, and extended for a further period of 5 years in 2008.  
  
The signing ceremony was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and witnessed by senior officials from the Ministry and officials of the Embassy of the United States of America in Colombo.  
  
END.

en.title: A special Reception held to celebrate the Chinese New Year and to introduce the New Chinese Ambassador
en.description: 28th January 2014, Male'; A special reception was held at the Traders Hotel today to celebrate the Chinese New Year and to introduce the New Chinese Ambassador to the Maldives, Mr. Wang Fukang Ambassador. The reception…
en.body:
28th January 2014, Male'; A special reception was held at the Traders Hotel today to celebrate the Chinese New Year and to introduce the New Chinese Ambassador to the Maldives, Mr. Wang Fukang Ambassador. The reception was inaugurated by Dr. Mohamed Waheedh Hassan and the chief guest was the Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Ms Dunya Maumoon.

The reception was attended by senior officials of the government, various diplomats residing in Maldives, high profile stakeholders of the Maldivian Tourism Industry and some Chinese citizens working and residing in the Maldives.  
  
In the speech delivered at the event by the Chinese Ambassador Mr. Wang Fukang, the Ambassador noted the close ties that exist between the two countries and assured China's firm commitment towards the development of Maldives.  
  
In the speech delivered by the Minster of Foreign Minister H.E Ms Dunya Maumoon, the Minister noted the assistance provided by China to the Maldives, in the most exigent of times, and noted the importance of the partnership that exist between the two countries. The Minister, further on, assured of the full support that would always be provided by Maldives to the China.  
  
The MNDF Band and Staff of the Chinese Embassy collaborated to present musical items at the reception. The event was concluded by a Dinner hosted in honor of the reception's guests.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Speech delivered by H.E. Ms.Dunya Maumoon, Foreign Minister of the Republic of Maldives, at the reception to mark Vin d' honneur in conjunction with the celebration of Chinese New Year
en.description: His Excellency Mr. Wang Fukang Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to the Republic of Maldives,
en.body:
His Excellency Mr. Wang Fukang Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to the Republic of Maldives,

Excellencies,  
  
Distinguished guests,  
  
Ladies and gentlemen,  
  
Good Evening….  
  
On behalf of the Government and people of the Maldives, and my own behalf I wish to extend, my warm felicitations and sincere good wishes to His Excellency Mr. Wang Fukang, Ambassador of China to the Maldives, for the appointment of His Excellency as the second resident Ambassador of China to the Maldives.  
  
Let me also take this opportunity to send warm greeting to everyone observing the Chinese New Year. This ancient annual festival unites people of Chinese heritage around the globe in a joyous celebration of hope and new beginning.  
  
There's a very deep and rich relationship between Maldives and China, as we take note of the 41 years of diplomatic relations between Maldives and China, I do wish profoundly that we continue to do everything we can to build the relationship between Maldives and China. It is a strong and vibrant relationship. Today, relations between the Maldives and China are founded on mutual respect, shared principles and values and common understanding on issues of global importance.  
  
Maldives has always looked to China as an invaluable friend whose contribution to the social, cultural and economic development of Maldives is immense. There's the great excitement about our economies. Some of the projects, some of the businesses underway are thrilling. There's so much that we share together. Trade between the Maldives and China has increased significantly in the past few years and China remains one of the largest trading partners of the Maldives.  
  
I have no doubt that the traditional bonds of friendship and cooperation that we have enjoyed over the past four decades will continue to grow and expand in the years to come. China continues to be a close partner of the Maldives in diverse spheres.  
  
I would like to take this opportunity to express our sincere gratitude and appreciation to the Government and people of China, for the warmth in the official ties, as well as the generosity and continued support for the Maldives. On behalf of the Government and the people of Maldives, I reassure that Maldives will always support the Government and people of China in every way possible.  
  
Once again, on this momentous occasion, let me convey best wishes for continued peace, prosperity and progress of the people of China.

en.title: President concludes State Visit to Sri Lanka
en.description: 23 January 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has arrived back in Male' on conclusion of his State Visit to Sri Lanka. The President and First Lady arrived this evening.
en.body:
23 January 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has arrived back in Male' on conclusion of his State Visit to Sri Lanka. The President and First Lady arrived this evening.

On arrival at the Ibrahim Nasir International Airport, the President briefed the local media on the successful visit, and said that his visit has strengthened further, the close relations between the Maldives and Sri Lanka.  
  
The President described Sri Lanka as the Maldives' closest neighbor, and highlighted the key areas of discussion during his trip, and the agreements that were signed between the two governments.  
  
Noting that the population of Maldivians residing in Sri Lanka was over 14000, the President briefed on the discussions held with the Sri Lankan government regarding the difficulties being faced by Maldivians in the areas of health, education, and in issuing dependent visa. He said that the Sri Lankan government has assured the Maldives' government that the concerns would be addressed, and favorable solutions found.  
  
President Yameen said that the government of Maldives has decided to allocate a land plot in Male', for the High Commission of Sri Lanka, as a gesture of friendship.  
  
The President further highlighted his meeting with the Arab diplomats in Sri Lanka. He said that it would further expand the cooperation between the Maldives and the Arab world.  
  
President Yameen also took some questions from the media, regarding his State Visit to Sri Lanka.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Sri Lankan President and First Lady officially welcome President Yameen and First Lady to Sri Lanka
en.description: 22 January 2014, Male';His Excellency President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Madam Fathimath Ibrahim have received a grand welcome from the Sri Lankan Government. The ceremony was held this afternoon at…
en.body:
22 January 2014, Male';His Excellency President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Madam Fathimath Ibrahim have received a grand welcome from the Sri Lankan Government. The ceremony was held this afternoon at the Presidential Secretariat of Sri Lanka.

President Yameen and Madam Fathimath Ibrahim were escorted to the Presidential Secretariat from Hilton Colombo, by ceremonial motorcycles and mounted escorts, along with some cultural performers.  
  
At the Presidential Secretariat President Yameen and the First Lady were officially received by President Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Madam Shiranthi Rajapaksa of Sri Lanka.  
  
When both the Presidents ascended the saluting dais, they received the presidential salute. Next the Sri Lankan Army fired a 21 gun salute in honour of President Yameen, followed by which President Yameen inspected a guard of honour accorded to him by the Sri Lankan Navy.  
  
At the official welcome ceremony, President Rajapaksa then proceeded to introduce to President Yameen and Madam Fathimath Ibrahim, the Sri Lankan dignitaries at the receiving line. President Yameen then introduced the Maldivian dignitaries to the Sri Lankan President and First Lady.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Important Agreements Signed between the Governments of Maldives and Sri Lanka
en.description: 22 January 2014, Male';Three very important agreements were signed today between the Governments of Maldives and Sri Lanka, as part of President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom's current visit to Sri Lanka.
en.body:
22 January 2014, Male';Three very important agreements were signed today between the Governments of Maldives and Sri Lanka, as part of President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom's current visit to Sri Lanka.

Following are the agreements that were signed:  
  
1. MoU on combating Transnational Crime and Developing Police Cooperation between Sri Lanka and the Maldives  
  
The agreement was signed by the Sri Lankan Inspector General of Police N.K. Illangakoon, and the Police Commissioner Hussain Waheed.  
  
2. MoU for Vocational Training and Skills Development between Sri Lanka and the Maldives  
  
The agreement was signed by the Minister of Youth Affairs and Skills Development of Sri Lanka, Dulles Alahapperuma, and the Minister of Foreign Affairs Dunya Maumoon.  
  
3. MoU on Sports Cooperation between Sri Lanka and Maldives  
  
The agreement was signed by the Minister of Sports of Sri Lanka, Mahindananda Aluthgamage, and the Minister at the President's Office Mohamed Hussain Shareef.  
  
President Yameen and President Mahinda Rajapaksa were in attendance at the signing ceremony.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Maldives and Sri Lanka Hold Official Talks
en.description: 22 January 2014, Male';The Government of Maldives and Sri Lanka have held official talks, led by President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and the Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa.
en.body:
22 January 2014, Male';The Government of Maldives and Sri Lanka have held official talks, led by President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and the Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa.

The President reiterated the government's commitment to enhance the welfare of the people, develop and diversify the economy, strengthen social cohesion within the country, and empower the youth.  
  
In his speech, the President expressed hopes that this visit would further strengthen and expand trade relations between the Maldives and Sri Lanka. He also assured the Sri Lankan President of Maldives' firm support to Sri Lanka at the international level.  
  
At the meeting, discussions were also held on the regional and international issues of mutual concern.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: President Yameen and First Lady meet Sri Lankan President and First Lady
en.description: 22 January 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Madam Fathimath Ibrahim have today met with President Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Madam Shiranthi Rajapaksa of Sri Lanka.
en.body:
22 January 2014, Male';President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and First Lady Madam Fathimath Ibrahim have today met with President Mahinda Rajapaksa and First Lady Madam Shiranthi Rajapaksa of Sri Lanka.

At the meeting held prior to the official talks between the two countries, President Yameen thanked President Rajapaksa, the Government, and the people of Sri Lanka, for extending the invitation to make the visit. The President highlighted the close bilateral relations between the Maldives and Sri Lanka.  
  
Speaking at the meeting, President Mahinda Rajapaksa expressed his appreciation to President Yameen and the First Lady on accepting the invitation. He also noted that the Maldives and Sri Lanka shared strong, brotherly bonds.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Sri Lankan External Affairs Minister pays a courtesy call on President Yameen
en.description: 21 January 2014, Male';The Minister of External Affairs of Sri Lanka, Hon. Prof. G. L. Peiris has paid a courtesy call on the President of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom. The meeting was held this…
en.body:
21 January 2014, Male';The Minister of External Affairs of Sri Lanka, Hon. Prof. G. L. Peiris has paid a courtesy call on the President of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom. The meeting was held this afternoon at the hotel in which the Maldivian President is residing at during his State Visit to Sri Lanka.

President Yameen and External Affairs Minister Peiris exchanged views on charting the way forward in further enhancing bilateral ties between the Maldives and Sri Lanka, during President Yameen's tenure of office. Highlighting the historical good neighbourly ties and mutual respect between the two countries, deliberations focused on advancing development cooperation and commercial interactions in the time ahead.  
  
Minister Peiris congratulated President Yameen on his elections triumph, and welcomed the prevalent peace and stability in the country since the change in leadership. He noted that Sri Lanka had personally experienced the transformation in economic fortunes associated with prolonged stability and domestic peace and harmony. He elaborated that, as such, the Sri Lankan Government had every confidence that President Yameen's aspirations for accelerated economic growth would materialize, particularly through a manifold increase in foreign investment targeted at the ambitious mega projects earmarked under the new administration's manifesto.  
  
President Yameen commended President Rajapaksa for his leadership and insight in bringing about a revolutionary change in the country's socioeconomic development. He assured Sri Lanka of the Maldives' continued steadfast support to Sri Lanka at international and regional forums of common membership.  
  
President Yameen noted the importance of forging stronger regional ties in improving collective bargaining in the international arena, and shared his vision of a prosperous South Asia. He also highlighted the need to increase bilateral cooperation in selected areas of development, including tourism, trade and fisheries.  
  
Minister G. L. Peiris spoke on the tremendous potential for increased trade and investment, which he noted would be of tremendous benefit to both countries. He also assured the Maldivian President of Sri Lanka's commitment to support the Maldives in key areas of development, including education and health.  
  
President Yameen briefed the Sri Lankan External Affairs Minister on the key objectives of his administration's foreign policy and requested for Sri Lankan government assistance in his quest to improve consular services for the large Maldivian community residing in Sri Lanka.  
  
President Yameen was accompanied at the call by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, Minister at the President's Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef, Minister of Tourism, Hon. Ahmed Adeeb Abdul Ghafoor, Maldivian High Commissioner in Sri Lanka, His Excellency Hussain Shihab, Foreign Secretary, Dr. Ali Naseer Mohamed and Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ms Farzana Zahir.  
  
Minister Peiris was joined at the call by the Senior Minister of Urban Affairs and Minister in Attendance for President Yameen's State Visit, Hon. A. H. M. Fowzie, Sri Lankan High Commissioner in the Maldives, His Excellency Dixon Dela, and Foreign Secretary, Ms Kshenuka Seneviratne.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: Sri Lanka's Minister of Industry and Commerce calls on President Yameen
en.description: 21 January 2014, Male'; The Minister of Industry and Commerce of Sri Lanka, Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen called on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this afternoon.
en.body:
21 January 2014, Male'; The Minister of Industry and Commerce of Sri Lanka, Hon. Rishad Bathiudeen called on President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this afternoon.

During the discussions held at the President's resident hotel in Sri Lanka, Minister Bathiudeen recalled the strong ties that President Yameen had cultivated with his predecessors, during President Yameen's tenure as Trade Minister of the Maldives in President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom's Cabinet. He noted that the President's vast experience in trade and commerce will undoubtedly raise interest among the business community in Sri Lanka towards expanding import-export ties with the Maldives.  
  
President Yameen noted the potential for further strengthening of trade ties between the Maldives and Sri Lanka, and pointed out that the high-level business forum held today with encouraging interest and participation by high-profile entrepreneurs from the two countries.  
  
President Yameen and Minister Bathiudeen discussed the importance of reviving the Sri Lanka-Maldives Joint Economic Commission at the earliest to identify further areas for cooperation and mutual benefit. He commended Sri Lanka's rapid socioeconomic development over the past seven years of President Mahinda Rajapaksa's leadership.  
  
President Yameen was joined at the call by the Minister at the President's Office, His Excellency Mohamed Hussain Shareef, Spokesperson at the President's Office, Mr. Ibrahim Muaz Ali and Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ms Farzana Zahir.  
  
Minister Bathiudeen was joined by the Deputy Minister of Industry and Commerce, Mr. V. A. D. Lakshman Wasantha Perera and senior officials of key state and private enterprises of Sri Lanka.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: President Yameen and First Lady depart on a State Visit to Sri Lanka
en.description: 21 January 2014, Male';His Excellency President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has this morning departed on a State Visit to Sri Lanka, on the invitation of President of Sri Lanka, H.E. Mahinda Rajapaksa. President Yameen…
en.body:
21 January 2014, Male';His Excellency President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has this morning departed on a State Visit to Sri Lanka, on the invitation of President of Sri Lanka, H.E. Mahinda Rajapaksa. President Yameen is accompanied by First Lady Madam Fathimath Ibrahim.

Meeting the local media at the Official Jetty prior to his departure, President Yameen said the purpose of the visit was to further strengthen the existing bilateral ties between the Maldives and Sri Lanka. Underscoring that Sri Lanka has always been the closest ally of the Maldives, President Yameen highlighted that four agreements on bilateral cooperation would be signed during his visit to Sri Lanka.  
  
During the three-day visit, President Yameen will hold one-to-one deliberations with President Rajapaksa on charting the course for future Maldives-Sri Lanka bilateral ties. An official Welcoming Ceremony will be held at the Presidential Secretariat. President Rajapaksa and Sri Lankan First Lady Madam Shirathi Rajapaksa will host President Yameen and First Lady Madam Fathimath Ibrahim for a State Luncheon at the President's House.  
  
President Yameen is accompanied by a high-level delegation that includes Hon. Qasim Ibrahim, Leader of the Jumhooree Party, Hon. Ahmed Siyam Mohamed, Leader of the Maldives Development Alliance, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Tourism, Hon. Ahmed Adheeb Abdul Ghafoor, Minister at the President's Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef, Vice President of the Progressive Party of Maldives (PPM), Hon. en.title: Foreign Ministers of Sri Lanka and the Maldives have Bilateral Discussions
en.description: 21 January 2014, Colombo; Professor G.L. Peiris, Minister of External Affairs, and Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, held bilateral discussions at the Ministry ofExternal Affairs on Tuesday.
en.body:
21 January 2014, Colombo; Professor G.L. Peiris, Minister of External Affairs, and Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, held bilateral discussions at the Ministry ofExternal Affairs on Tuesday.

These discussions reflected the special and warm relationship between the two countries.  
  
Prof. Peiris, welcoming Ms. Maumoon on her first official visit to Sri Lanka as Foreign Minister, said that the recent political transition which took place in the Maldives, indicated the maturity and foresight of all parties concerned.  
  
The two Ministers agreed on the need to intensify discussions within the already established mechanisms for structured bilateral dialogue.  
  
The two Ministers expressed satisfaction that Memoranda of Understanding on a variety of issues such as health, youth and skills development, sports, combating crime and police training would be signed between the two countries during the State visit of President Abdulla Yameen of the Maldives to Sri Lanka.  
  
Among the specific issues discussed were co-operation in education, food security, economic and trade relations, supply of fruit and vegetables to the Maldives through Mattala airport, employment and collaboration in the defence and fisheries sectors.  
  
Prof. Peiris gave his counterpart in the new government of the Maldives a comprehensive update on political and economic developments in Sri Lanka.  
  
The Ministers agreed that the vital interests of both countries would be served by the closest co-operation between them.  
  
ENDS.

en.title: President Yameen launches the Foreign Policy of Maldives
en.description: 20 January 2014, Male, President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has today launched the Foreign Policy of the Maldives. The ceremony was held this afternoon at the President's Office.
en.body:
20 January 2014, Male, President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has today launched the Foreign Policy of the Maldives. The ceremony was held this afternoon at the President's Office.

Highlighting the strategies set in the new Foreign Policy, the President noted that it focused on enhancing national sovereignty and protecting the Islamic identity of the country.  
  
  
  
Speaking in this regard, the President noted that the 26 July 2015 would mark the golden jubilee of the Maldives' independence, and that a strong and strategic policy was vital for the Maldives to maintain peace and stability.  
  
  
  
Highlighting the many similarities in his Foreign Policy to that of former President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom, President Yameen said that the newly formulated government policy promoted sovereign equality of States in accordance with international law, and gave emphasis to consolidating friendship with all countries based on mutual respect. He also stressed that bilateral collaborations must be lead through diplomatic dialogue, and that each country was entitled to sovereign equality.  
  
  
  
Underlining that the main objective of his foreign policy was to increase opportunities for the economic advancement of Maldivians, the President said that in today's world, an independent foreign policy could only be employed by becoming an economically sufficient, and resilient nation.  
  
  
  
Stating that the another important goal of the government's Foreign Policy was providing quality consular services for Maldivians, the President said that the new Foreign Policy aims to conclude visa waiver agreements with countries most frequently visited by Maldivians. He said that the government was responsible to facilitate the consular protection guaranteed by international laws, for all Maldivians travelling and residing abroad.  
  
  
  
Speaking at the function, President Yameen also said that the government was working on a Foreign Service Act in order to make the Maldivian consular service more result oriented, and to promote efficiency and professionalism in the service. He said that the government would submit the bill for the parliament's approval, in its first hundred days.  
  
  
  
In his speech, the President further said that a Foreign Service Institute has been established on 16 January 2014, under the administration of the Ministry of Foreign Affair. The mandate for the institution includes human resource development in the foreign service sector, enrichment of the foreign policy, and conducting pertinent academic research.  
  
  
  
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, and Minister at the President's Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef also spoke at the ceremony.

en.title: Local Council Elections held in the Maldives
en.description: 19 January 2014, Male'; Local Council Elections in the Maldives was held yesterday. Elections Commission of the Maldives announced that there were a total 240,220 eligible voters for the election.
en.body:
19 January 2014, Male'; Local Council Elections in the Maldives was held yesterday. Elections Commission of the Maldives announced that there were a total 240,220 eligible voters for the election.

A total of 2,462 candidates participated in the elections, and from among them, 1,118 candidates are to be elected to the Island, Atoll and City Councils. This includes 975 candidates that are to be elected to the Island councils, 120 to the Atoll councils, 11 to the Male City Council and 6 to the Addu City Council. Preliminary results of the elections are expected to be announced sometime today.  
  
According to the Elections Commission, 464 ballot boxes were placed for the elections, including the 6 that were placed overseas. From the ballot boxes that were placed overseas, 2 were placed in Colombo, Sri Lanka; 2 in Thiruvananthapuram, India and 2 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.  
  
ENDS.

en.body:
14 January 2014,Male'; Mr. Abdullah Hameed has been appointed as the new Ambassador-at-Large at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The appointment was made by H. E. President Yameen Abdul Gayoom on 8th January 2014.

Mr. Hameed has served at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for 17 years. He first joined the Ministry as the Chief of Protocol in May 1991 and had held the post for 15 years at the rank of a Deputy Minister. On 7th December 2006, Mr. Hameed was appointed as Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs. After almost two and a half years of service in the said post, Mr. Hameed was then appointed as the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs on 14thAugust 2008.  
  
Prior to his appointment as Ambassador-at-Large, Mr. Hameed had served as the Honorary Consul of Seychelles to the Maldives.  
  
Minister of Foreign Affairs Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon conveyed her felicitations to Mr. Hameed for his appointment.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs welcomes the enactment of the Right to Information Act
en.description: 13 January 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs H. E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon has welcomed the enactment of the Right to Information Act (RTIA). President Abdulla Yameen, on 12th January 2014, ratified the RTIA, which was…
en.body:
13 January 2014, Male'; Minister of Foreign Affairs H. E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon has welcomed the enactment of the Right to Information Act (RTIA). President Abdulla Yameen, on 12th January 2014, ratified the RTIA, which was passed by the Parliament on 29thDecember 2013, during the 22nd sitting of its third session

The RTIA, with its underlying objective of holding government bodies to account and establishing means for the administration of such in the most transparent manner, ascertains the right of individual to acquire and receive governmental information and prescribes the limits in the exercise of the right.  
  
  
  
Namely, the RTIA expressly stipulates the right of individual to acquire and receive information underthe authority of the government, establishes exclusive circumstances under which such rights are exempted,lays down procedures for balancing public interest against potential harm in the disclosure of information under such circumstances, provides a supporting framework for the dissemination of governmental information on a wide scale, provides the right of individual to ascertain and rectify any information regarding the person held under the authority of the government and provides for the establishment of a regulatory regime in respect of the forgoing matters.  
  
  
  
The RTIA also prescribes to establish an Information Officer at every government office and establishes an Information Commissioner's Office to be headed by an Information Commissioner, appointed under the authority of the Parliament.  
  
  
  
The RTIA will come into force, six month from the date of its ratification.  
  
  
  
END.

en.description: 9 January 2014, Male'; The Embassy of China in Maldives has officially opened the Visa Section today. The Visa Section was jointly opened by Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs and by His…
en.body:
9 January 2014, Male'; The Embassy of China in Maldives has officially opened the Visa Section today. The Visa Section was jointly opened by Her Excellency Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs and by His Excellency Mr. Wang Fukang, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to the Maldives.

Speaking at the ceremony, Minister Dunya expressed her gratitude to the Government of China for opening the Visa Section of the Chinese Embassy in Maldives, and noted the significance of the facility's role in furthering trade and investment, between the two countries.  
  
Ambassador Wang in his speech, thanked the Government of Maldives for the support and assistance it has provided in enabling the Chinese Embassy to establish its Visa Section today, and noted the previous hurdles they had faced in its endeavor to set up such, since the establishment of the Embassy in 2011. In conclusion, the Ambassador stated that he hoped more Maldivians would take this opportunity to visit and study in China.  
  
Senior Officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Department of Immigration and Emigration and from the Business sector participated in this event.  
  
ENDS.

en.description: 07th January 2014, Male'; The New Ambassador of France accredited to the Maldives, H. E. Mr. Jean-Paul Monchau paid a courtesy call on H. E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs today.
en.body:
07th January 2014, Male'; The New Ambassador of France accredited to the Maldives, H. E. Mr. Jean-Paul Monchau paid a courtesy call on H. E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, Minister of Foreign Affairs today.

During the meeting, held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Minister congratulated Ambassador Monchau on the commencement of his term.  
  
Ambassador Monchau expressed his commitment to working with the Government of Maldives on strengthening the relations between the two countries.  
  
Minister Dunya, noted the close bilateral relations between the two countries, and expressed confidence in further strengthening the ties during Ambassador Monchau's tenure.  
  
The Minister and the Ambassador also discussed about opportunities for expanding relations between the two countries. In this regard, they highlighted climate change, tourism and fisheries as areas of cooperation.  
  
The Minister also reiterated President Yameen's development priorities in areas of youth, economy, and infrastructure and women empowerment.  
  
The meeting was also attended by Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, H. E. Ms. Fathimath Inaya, Minister's Communication Director, Mr. Zaaid Ahmed and Head of Europe Desk Ms. Aminath Guraysha.

en.body:
06 January 2014, Male';New Ambassador of France accredited to the Maldives, Mr. Jean-Paul Monchau presented his letter of credence to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, this morning.

At the ceremony held at the President's Office to present credentials, President Yameen congratulated Ambassador Monchau on the commencement of his term.  
  
Meeting the new Ambassador after the ceremonial presentation of credentials, President Yameen expressed hope that the cordial relations that exist between the two countries would further enhance during the tenure of Ambassador Monchau.  
  
Speaking at the meeting, President expressed his gratitude for the Government of France's continued support and assistance to the socio-economic development of the Maldives. He especially highlighted the developmental assistances received from France following the 2004 tsunami. He also recalled the pioneering contributions of France in the development of the country's award-winning tourism industry, and expressed his hope that the Maldives would continue to feature among preferred destinations of French tourists.  
  
Ambassador Monchau highlighted ongoing efforts to facilitate Maldivians to learn French as a useful business language, particularly for use in the tourism sector.  
  
At the meeting, the President and the Ambassador also discussed bilateral relations and ways to further strengthen ties. In this regard, discussions were held on extending cooperation between the two countries in issues related to climate change and in developing tourism and fisheries sectors.  
  
Ambassador Monchau reassured President Yameen of his Government's continuous support and cooperation to the Maldives.  
  
President Yameen was joined at the call by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon and Minister at the President's Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef. Ambassador Monchau was joined at the call by the Honorary Consul of France in the Maldives, Mr. Ismail Wafir.  
  
ENDS.
